solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son quietly studied magazine feature

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A boy has been poring over an article in a magazine, without making a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-page article or layout across facing pages in a magazine is called a spread.

clue.text: Disinfectant fluid no help

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that some cleaning liquid is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' looks like part of the description of the disinfectant, but it signals a rearrangement of NOHELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, also called carbolic acid, was the antiseptic Lister used to sterilise surgical instruments.

clue.text: High-spirited former soldier grabs cheap taxi

indicators.note: one part grabbing another holds it inside, so the soldier's letters wrap around the taxi

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former
a soldier ant is a kind of worker ant, so ant is the usual crossword soldier
Uber is the app-based taxi service sold as cheaper than a cab

explanation.surface: A lively veteran seizes a budget ride-share car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former soldier' reads as one veteran but splits in two around the taxi, which 'grabs' places in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant describes someone full of energy and cheerful excitement, which is what high-spirited means.

clue.text: Dunderhead is on schedule to make speech

parts.note: read as 'Dunder head', the head of the word Dunder, its first letter D
a course, as in a course of treatment or lectures, is a planned schedule

explanation.surface: A fool is lined up to give an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like an insult but splits into 'Dunder' plus 'head', giving its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or written treatment of a subject, so it can be a speech.

clue.text: Virago shows impulsive desire in hot island

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it, here inside the island's name

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
in Freudian psychology the id is the source of instinctive, impulsive drives

explanation.surface: A domineering woman reveals her urges on a sweltering island.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a bossy, bad-tempered and overbearing woman, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Waller took top tip from Roach — piano's inside

parts.note: had can mean took, as in 'had a biscuit'

indicators.note: the top tip of a word in a down clue is its first letter
the inside of a word is all its letters except the two ends

explanation.surface: A man building a wall took the best advice from a Roach, with a piano installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waller' is the definition: Emperor Hadrian built the wall across northern England. The middle of PIANO is IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor ordered the great frontier wall in northern Britain, so he is jokingly the Waller.

clue.text: Villain has non-British accent

indicators.note: non-British means without B, the abbreviation for British, so B is taken out

parts.note: a brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish or Scottish

explanation.surface: The bad guy in a film speaks with a foreign accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-British' removes B from BROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest, unprincipled man, which is what a villain is.

clue.text: Maybe Auskerry has tenant?

definitions.meaning: Auskerry is a small uninhabited island in Orkney, an example of a tiny island
a property that has a tenant ... out; split the answer as ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into IS LET, a property that has a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Auskerry is a little Orkney island, and a small island is an example of this word.

clue.text: Announces scion delivered in travelling up

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out loud, so the words that follow are given by their sound

parts.note: a scion is a descendant, an heir; a delivered baby has been born

explanation.surface: A proclamation that a royal baby has been delivered while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIR BORN said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that has taken off and is in flight, moving up through the sky, is said to be in the air.

clue.text: Ravel Preludes caused dislike

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters of the next word are rearranged; the surface uses the French composer

explanation.surface: Some piano preludes by the French composer Ravel provoked distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the composer, but it signals that PRELUDES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse someone is to fill them with disgust, so repulsed in the past tense means caused dislike.

clue.text: Bond role in abundance

definitions.meaning: Pussy ... is the pilot in the James Bond film Goldfinger, played by Honor Blackman
... follows a noun to mean in great quantity, as in 'prizes ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Placed after a noun, the word means plentiful, in large numbers, matching in abundance.

clue.text: Short coat for dance in Madrid

definitions.meaning: a cropped jacket ending above the waist, open at the front
a Spanish dance in triple time, fitting the Madrid setting

explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is both a cropped open jacket and a Spanish dance in triple time, famous from Ravel.

clue.text: Forming concepts in hide at Iona

indicators.note: the letters are found in the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Thinking things up while tucked away on the Scottish island of Iona.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideation is the psychological term for the process of forming ideas.

clue.text: Deadly snake with stinger losing weight

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so the weight's letter goes from the insect

parts.note: a wasp is an insect with a sting

explanation.surface: A venomous snake joins a stinging insect in a tale about losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes W out of WASP.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a venomous Egyptian cobra, the snake said to have killed Cleopatra.

clue.text: Barman and former drinkers right about police state?

parts.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, AA, is the fellowship of people who have given up drinking
on can mean about, as in 'a talk on birds'
a cop is a police officer
a land is a nation or state

explanation.surface: A bartender teams up with recovering alcoholics in a police state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender: music is written in bars, so a composer is a bar man. Aaron Copland was the American composer of Appalachian Spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is written in bars, so a composer is playfully a man of bars, and Copland composed.

clue.text: Start to speak pompously having necked one drink

indicators.note: necking a drink is swallowing it, so the drink and the one go inside the speaking

parts.note: to orate is to make a pompous, long-winded speech
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone begins a grand speech after downing a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having necked' signals that one drink is swallowed by the pompous speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being, the same as to start.

clue.text: Grilled dish needs no Moselle in cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes things up, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe insists the grill dish uses no German Moselle wine in the cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in cooking' rearranges NOMOSELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a flatfish often served grilled, so it is a grilled dish.

clue.text: Margins trimmed, act as soon as Neo has plan

indicators.note: trimming a word's margins removes its first and last letters, leaving the centre

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, as in 'once you arrive'
Neo is the setter, who refers to themselves as I
've is the short form of have, as in I've

explanation.surface: A director trims the edges of a scene and acts as soon as the setter has a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of ACT is C. Neo is this puzzle's setter, so the setter's name stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceive a scheme is to devise or think it up, which is what planning it means.

clue.text: Free time promised in afternoon

indicators.note: freeing the letters lets them loose to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was promised some free time later in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like part of 'free time' but signals that TIMEPROMISED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, shortened to p.m., means after midday, so it marks a time in the afternoon.

clue.text: Something's dealt with

indicators.note: read as 'has', the first word has the answer's letters held inside it

explanation.surface: A short remark that some matter has been sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Something's' as 'Something has': the word has the letters running inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or a problem is to deal with it, so met is the past tense.

clue.text: One in clique imprisoned at Broadmoor finally

parts.note: someone inside is in prison

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gang member is locked up at Broadmoor, the high-security psychiatric hospital in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a member of a closed group with access to its secrets, one in a clique.

clue.text: Bird or carp in great river

definitions.note: two senses: a game bird, and a verb meaning to complain

parts.note: GR is an abbreviation for great
the Ouse is a river in England (there are several)

explanation.surface: A bird or a fish in a big river, carp being a fish as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the fish but here is the verb meaning complain.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a moorland game bird, and to grouse is to grumble, the same as to carp.

clue.text: Prickly plant in a container like this

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A thorny plant grows in a pot just like this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus, bear's breeches, has spiny leaves, and its leaf decorates Corinthian columns.

clue.text: Designated area in North Sea

indicators.note: the area's letter goes in among the other two pieces

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A zone in the North Sea has been officially marked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Sea' looks like one body of water but is two pieces, N and MED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be named for a role is to be designated or appointed to it.

clue.text: Share hole where fool incarcerates fifty

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to imprison, so the fool's letters hold the fifty inside

parts.note: to have someone on is to fool them; have alone can mean deceive
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A golfer splits a hole with a fool who locks up fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, two players who take the same score on a hole are said to share it, using this verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a hole is split when both sides take the same number of strokes, so neither wins it.

clue.text: Shun Italian man denied introduction

indicators.note: denying a word its introduction removes its first letter

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a gentleman, sir

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman is snubbed when nobody introduces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied introduction' takes S from the start of SIGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to refuse to notice them, which is how you shun them.

clue.text: Gloomy sergeant major in control

indicators.note: the sergeant major's letters are placed in the control

parts.note: a dial is a knob or control on a device

explanation.surface: A miserable sergeant major is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in control' looks like a description of the officer's authority, but 'in' is a placement signal and 'control' a knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means depressingly dark or dreary, a close synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Agile duo animated in discussion

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nimble pair gets lively in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges AGILEDUO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation or exchange of views between two or more parties.

clue.text: Top property Balmoral perhaps

parts.note: the head is the top of something
gear means belongings or personal property

explanation.surface: A prime royal estate, perhaps the Scottish castle of Balmoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balmoral' suggests the royal castle, but it is also a flat Scottish bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a flat Scottish bonnet, an example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: Diocese no longer safe when leader deposed

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer

indicators.note: deposing the leader removes the first letter

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, so a safebreaker is a peterman

explanation.surface: A church diocese is no longer secure after its head is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leader deposed' takes P from PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter in Devon is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, so its see is a diocese.
